title: Admin Companion: guided fallback orchestration & autopilot throttling
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: oncall engineers and first-line support frequently perform the same three remediation patterns when facing degraded inference capacity: scale up/burst, switch to low-cost model variants, and enable temporary KV/prefix cache bypasses. These steps are error-prone and slow under pressure.

Goal: build an 'Admin Companion' microservice and UI that exposes guided, auditable remediation flows (runbooks-as-tasks) for support. The Companion should offer a constrained set of safe actions (autopilot throttling, guided fallback orchestration, pre-flight checks, and one-click rollbacks) and integrate with runtime controls (routing, model variants, autoscale policies).

Scope: implement backend orchestration, a lightweight console panel in the Console (per-route 'Quick Remediate' panel), telemetry hooks, and an audit log. Provide 3 canonical runbook flows: 1) latency spike mitigation (throttle & route), 2) degraded-quality failover (model variant swap + cache reset), 3) transient overload (burst reserve + request-shed).

Out of scope: full RBAC redesign, on-prem packaging, or replacing existing autoscaler. Those will be handled as follow-ups.

Success metrics: mean time to remediate for targeted incidents reduced by 40%, 95th percentile time for runbook completion under 3 minutes, and zero accidental irreversible changes in first three weeks after rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Backend service exposes a safe, idempotent task API for the three canonical flows
Console panel renders runbook options with pre-checks and a detailed preview of the actions and impact
All actions are logged in an append-only audit stream with user, timestamp, and request context
Telemetry emits per-step latency, error rate, and outcome (success/failure/rollback) to the ops dashboard
Playbook runs support dry-run mode and require explicit confirmation for stateful operations
Integration tests cover end-to-end flow against a staging runtime and mock autoscaler
tasks: Design API contract for Task Runner including input schema, idempotency token, and audit metadata
Prototype Console panel wireframe and copy for operator guidance (link PRD in links)
Implement orchestration worker with step-level rollback handlers and circuit-breaker guards
Add runtime connectors: routing-policy toggle, model-variant swap endpoint, cache flush endpoint
Hook telemetry: step durations, step failures, operator ID, incident link, and pre/post SLO snapshots
Create integration test harness (staging runtime + autoscaler simulator)
Security review and KMS key scoping for audit logs
Canary rollout to internal ops team and collect feedback for two weeks
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: operator uses Companion to perform unsafe sequence leading to wider outage -> Mitigation: enforce conservative defaults, require two-step confirmation for any action that changes autoscaling or model variant for more than N routes
Risk: telemetry missing context for root-cause analysis -> Mitigation: include route, model version, tokenized sample prompt, and pre-run SLO snapshot in telemetry payloads
Risk: race between autoscaler and manual burst -> Mitigation: implement optimistic locking and an allowlist for autoscaler overrides during a Companion action
Risk: audit log integrity -> Mitigation: write audit events to append-only stream with signature and backfill to secure storage
links: Incident template and playbook canonicalization notes: https://docs.redwood.ai/ops/playbooks/canonical
